prompt: Write an email to a colleague about the anniversary of a public website your team runs. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Our site turns 10 next month: let's plan something

Hi Jordan,

I hope your week is going well. I wanted to flag something that's been on my mind: the public website turns ten years old on November 18. That's a real milestone for a project that began as a small experiment, and I think we should mark it properly.

When I looked back through the archives, I was struck by how far things have come. The first version was a handful of static pages, hosted on a single server, with a contact form that broke whenever someone used an apostrophe. Today we serve several hundred thousand visitors a month, support four languages, and meet accessibility standards we didn't even know to aim for back then. Much of that is thanks to the people on our team, past and present, who kept showing up to improve it.

I'd like us to do three things.

First, a short retrospective post on the site itself. Nothing flashy: a timeline of major changes, a few screenshots of earlier designs, and some thanks to the contributors. I'm happy to draft it if you can help me dig up the old screenshots. I believe some are in the shared drive under "Design Archive," though the folder structure is a bit of a maze.

Second, a small internal gathering. Maybe a lunch or a virtual coffee hour where we can reflect on what worked, what didn't, and what we want the next decade to look like. I'd especially like to invite former team members, since several of them built foundations we still rely on.

Third, and I think most valuable, a candid look at our technical debt. Anniversaries are a natural prompt for taking stock. We still have a few legacy components that make updates harder than they should be, and I'd like us to set aside time to decide which ones deserve attention in the coming year. I don't want this to feel like a chore, so I'm thinking of framing it as a "gift to our future selves" kind of exercise.

Could you let me know whether you're up for this, and whether you have thoughts on timing? If we want the blog post live on the 18th, we'd need a draft by early November, which gives us about two weeks. I'm also open to hearing if you think this is too much and we should scale back.

Also, if you remember any funny stories from the early days, send them my way. I'd love to include a couple. I vaguely recall an incident involving a homepage banner and a misplaced emoji, but I may be misremembering.

Thanks so much, and let me know when you have a few minutes to chat.

Best,
[name]
